messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: P1 - high 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-west1). Alert RNW-5082. Current symptom: ~12% error rate, spike started ~02:58 UTC. Pager: @maria.

maria (oncall): ack'd, joining bridge now. putting out brief: investigating request failures and increased latency for hosted API in us-west1. Hypothesis queue: kernel mismatch after recent runtime deploy / KV cache exhaustion / autoscaler flapping.

oliver (eng-sre): I can see repeated `ELIF` OOM traces in the runtime logs around 02:56-02:59. Pasting tail:```\n[02:58:11.234] runtime: failed to allocate KV cache shard: OOM\n[02:58:11.237] runtime: fallback to sync path, increased latency\n[02:58:12.001] 503 POST /v1/generate 127.0.0.1 - 0.21s\n```

mike (infra): repro-ing load locally against the same build (sha: b4f9c2a). I see degraded throughput on host gpu-uw1-37; dmesg shows kernel driver warnings around the same time. Dropping a quick `ssh` log:```\nMar 15 02:58:09 gpu-uw1-37 kernel: nvidia: GPU page allocation failed\nMar 15 02:58:10 gpu-uw1-37 runtime: reclaiming caches\n```

kevin (swe): timeline notes (tentative):
- 02:45 UTC: rolling canary deploy of runtime v1.13.7 -> 10% traffic
- 02:55 UTC: canary autoscaler scaled from 2->8 pods
- 02:56 UTC: first 5xx observed in canary
- 02:58 UTC: error spike hits main pool, pager triggered
Can someone confirm if config for `kv_cache_size` changed in the deploy?

sara (pm): do we have customer impact numbers? Need to draft status page message if customer-facing. Which tenants/routes were hit?

emily (support): Support funnel: 6 tickets opened in last 20m referencing 503s, 3 SOC threads flagged. Affected customers include two mid-market tenants using streaming endpoints. I'll attach ticket IDs in the bridge.

oliver (eng-sre): hypothesis list (rolling):
1) regression in kernel selection logic in v1.13.7 causing memory pressure on certain GPU drivers
2) KV cache sizing/eviction bug under churn -> OOMs
3) autoscaler mis-scaling leading to hot nodes
Please add/confirm. We should collect: runtime logs, dmesg, deploy diff, autoscaler events.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan (immediate):
- temporarily route traffic away from us-west1 to us-west2 for non-low-latency customers
- scale up dedicated GPU pool by +20% (ops)
- rollback canary to v1.13.6 if we see no improvement in 10m
I'm drafting status page now. Draft below — please sanity-check language:```\nStatus: Partial service disruption impacting text generation in US-West (ongoing)\nImpact: Some requests return 5xx errors or experience elevated latency. Error rate peak ~12% at 02:58 UTC; mitigation in progress.\nNext update: in 30 minutes or when we have a significant change.\nWorkaround: Traffic steering to alternate region for select customers; automatic retries recommended.\n```

statuspage-bot: Saved draft to staging: https://status.redwood.example/drafts/RNW-5082 (access: eng+ops).

sara (pm): language looks good. Suggest we include customer guidance for retry/backoff and note we're prioritizing high-SLA tenants for regional failover. Also set update cadence to 30m initially. Who owns stakeholder comms? @sara + @maria?

mike (infra): Mitigation applied: scaled pool +patched kernel selection fallback to conservative path on gpu-uw1-*. Commands run:```\n# scale command\nredwood infra scale-gpu-pool --pool us-west1-main --delta +4\n# toggle conservative kernels\nredwood runtime set-flag --kernel-fallback conservative\n```\nI pushed a quick metric: error rate dropped to 6.1% within 4m of scaling.

oliver (eng-sre): pulling exact grep for OOMs:```\n$ grep -E "failed to allocate|OOM" /var/log/runtime/*.log | wc -l\n142\n$ grep "failed to allocate" /var/log/runtime/2026-03-15.log | head -5\n[02:56:59] failed to allocate KV cache shard id=7 size=128MB\n[02:57:12] failed to allocate KV cache shard id=7 size=128MB\n```
This points at repeated allocation failures on the same shard id — suggests a leak or eviction bug.

maria (oncall): action items:
- oliver, attach full runtime logs & deploy diff to the incident doc (R/W on the bridge folder)
- mike, keep scaling until error <1% or until pool capacity limits reached
- kevin, start a bisect of the 1.13.7 changes focused on kernel selection + cache sizing flags
- emily, initial customer note ready to send once we confirm mitigation working
I propose we update status page now with: "Mitigation in progress; error rates decreasing; targeted failover for high-SLA tenants."

emily (support): initial customer note (template) — please review before I send to affected customers:```\nSubject: Service disruption affecting text generation in US-West (Mar 15)\nWe are investigating increased errors and latency for text generation in our US-West region. Our engineers are actively mitigating (traffic steering and scaling). We will provide updates every 30 minutes. No data loss has been detected at this time.\nIf you need immediate assistance we can route your traffic to US-West2.\n```

kevin (swe): started bisect: reproducing locally against kernels changed in c3b2 -> b4f9c2a. I'll post PR references and test logs.

maria (oncall): immediate status: after scaling + kernel fallback, error rate now 1.8% and trending down. Keeping oncall until we hit <0.5% and confirm stability for 30m. We're going to keep the status page live and post an update in 30 minutes. If we can confirm root cause (KV eviction leak in 1.13.7), plan is to rollback and issue a patch release.

oliver (eng-sre): uploading logs and autoscaler events to incident doc now, link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/RNW-5082/logs (ops access). Also attaching the `nvml` driver traces that show memory pressure spikes.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. Quick comms plan:
- 03:35 UTC: Post status page update (maria)
- 03:45 UTC: Stakeholder email to sales + CS with list of impacted tenants (sara + emily)
- 04:00 UTC: Decision point for rollback vs patch (kevin + oliver + mike)
I'll leave this thread open for timeline additions and log snippets. If anyone adds new tickets or findings, paste here so I can include in the post-incident timeline.

emily (support): sending initial customer messages to the 2 affected mid-market tenants now, CC-ing sara.

maria (oncall): last update in this thread: mitigation applied and verified — error rate down from 12% -> 1.8%, support tickets created: 6, affected heavy-streaming tenants: 2. Handing to follow-up owner for RCA: kevin + oliver. Leaving oncall at 04:10 UTC.
